title: Meet Priya
body: Priya reviews charts for an 8-provider family medicine group. Here is her morning before and after this tool.

title: Every chart, not a sample
body: Every visit from the last three business days has a first-pass review. Priya no longer picks a third of them at random.

title: One history per chart
body: The review findings, provider messages, and every status change for a chart, in order.

title: A conflict, caught the next morning
body: The note says lisinopril was stopped, but the medication list still shows it with a refill queued. This chart was flagged before the refill went out.

title: The deadline is on screen
body: A live countdown to the correction deadline, so no one has to track it in a spreadsheet.

title: Priya still decides
body: The medication list isn't changed and the chart doesn't go to billing until Priya reviews the fix and approves it herself.

title: The numbers that matter
body: Charts reviewed, flag rate, overdue flags, and time to resolve, all worked out from the chart data on this screen.

title: How this would be built
body: A nightly job reads closed encounters from the existing EMR, sends minimum-necessary note text to Claude under a BAA for review, and writes flags to this app. Chart changes go back to the EMR only after staff approval.
